question:
Patient note:
A 19-year-old man with relapsed acute lymphoblastic leukemia who completed his second cycle of blinatumomab two weeks ago and remains on daily oral prednisone 40 mg as graft-versus-host prophylaxis after a matched-sibling stem-cell transplant six months earlier was brought by ambulance from his university dormitory after his roommate found him curled on the bathroom floor complaining of shaking chills and a pounding headache; they reported that over the preceding 24 hours he had felt progressively febrile, vomited twice, and grown short of breath walking the ten yards to the communal sink. Paramedics arrived eight minutes after the 911 call and recorded an axillary temperature of 104.2 °F, a thready radial pulse in the 130s, and oxygen saturation in the low 80s on room air; they applied a high-flow nasal cannula set to 60 L min⁻¹ with a blender dialed to 70 % but administered no intravenous fluids, antibiotics, antipyretics, steroids, vasopressors, bronchodilators, or insulin en route. Within the emergency department resuscitation bay—before any hospital therapy was started and with the oxygen device unchanged—triage documented a core temperature measured rectally at 40.1 °C, non-invasive blood pressure cycling reproducibly at 108⁄61 mm Hg, a sinus tachycardia of 136 beats min⁻¹ on three-lead telemetry, and a visibly labored respiratory rate counted over a full minute at 39 breaths min⁻¹ with pronounced intercostal retractions. The patient opened his eyes only to loud verbal stimulus, uttered clipped phrases that were occasionally confused for time, and withdrew purposefully from painful nail-bed pressure, establishing a Glasgow Coma Score of 12 in the absence of sedatives, alcohol, or head trauma. Skin examination revealed flushed cheeks, generalized diaphoresis, and scattered petechiae over both shins; capillary refill was roughly three seconds, distal pulses were rapid but palpable, and there was no peripheral edema. Neck veins were flat at 30°, carotid upstrokes were brisk, and heart auscultation uncovered a rapid regular rhythm with no murmurs or rubs. Lung fields transmitted coarse crackles most prominently over the right middle zone, and percussion was mildly dull at the posterior bases; breath sounds were diminished but present throughout. The abdomen was soft with mild epigastric tenderness and active bowel sounds, and the transplanted right iliac crest scar from marrow harvest was well healed without erythema. There was no costovertebral angle tenderness, and bladder palpation was unremarkable. A right radial arterial puncture performed six minutes after stretcher placement while the fraction of inspired oxygen remained 73 % yielded a pH of 7.32; the blood-gas analyzer displayed an alveolar-to-arterial oxygen gradient of 167 mm Hg and a PaCO₂ of 34 mm Hg. End-tidal capnography read 32 mm Hg, validating effective ventilation despite tachypnea. Concurrent point-of-care chemistry returned sodium 118 mmol L⁻¹, potassium 5.9 mmol L⁻¹, chloride 92 mmol L⁻¹, bicarbonate 20 mmol L⁻¹, glucose 132 mg dL⁻¹, blood urea nitrogen 18 mg dL⁻¹, and serum creatinine 1.2 mg dL⁻¹—the latter matching his oncology clinic baseline from the previous week and arguing against renal injury; he likewise carries no prior diagnosis of chronic kidney disease or need for renal replacement therapy. A complete blood count drawn from the same syringe demonstrated white blood cells 24 200 mm³ with 85 % neutrophils and 3 % bands, hematocrit 43 %, hemoglobin 14.2 g dL⁻¹, and platelets 68 000 µL⁻¹. Venous lactate measured 3.6 mmol L⁻¹ at the bedside. Plain-film chest radiography obtained before any antimicrobial or steroid dosing revealed patchy right-perihilar consolidation with blurring of the right heart border and no overt effusion; the mediastinal silhouette was normal, and there were no lines or tubes present. Focused cardiac ultrasound showed a small but vigorously contracting left ventricle and an inferior vena cava measuring 1.3 cm that collapsed more than 50 % with inspiration, suggesting relative intravascular depletion rather than overload. Twelve-lead electrocardiography printed during the arterial draw depicted sinus tachycardia at 136 beats min⁻¹, PR interval 150 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 430 ms, and no acute ischemic changes. A urine sample obtained by straight catheterization produced 40 mL of concentrated amber fluid with a specific gravity of 1.027; dipstick was negative for ketones, leukocyte esterase, or nitrites. Importantly, from dormitory discovery through the conclusion of the initial intensive-care handoff—a span of roughly thirty minutes—the patient received no crystalloid infusion, no empiric antibiotics, no antipyretics, no vasopressors, no insulin, and no bronchodilators; the only ongoing intervention remained the high-flow nasal cannula delivering 73 % oxygen. Because there had been no operative procedure preceding this episode, the forthcoming intensive-care admission was categorized as a nonoperative medical transfer of an immunosuppressed host with presumed community-acquired pneumonia complicated by marked hyperpyrexia, profound hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, leukocytosis, and early hypoxemic respiratory compromise reflected by the contemporaneously captured values—temperature 40.1 °C, systolic pressure 108 mm Hg, diastolic pressure 61 mm Hg, pulse 136 beats min⁻¹, respirations 39 min⁻¹, arterial pH 7.32, serum sodium 118 mmol L⁻¹, potassium 5.9 mmol L⁻¹, creatinine 1.2 mg dL⁻¹, hematocrit 43 %, white blood cell count 24 200 mm³, fraction of inspired oxygen 73 %, and alveolar-to-arterial gradient 167 mm Hg.

Question: What is the patient's APACHE II score?
solution:
APACHE II adds acute physiology points, age points, and chronic health points. Using the available admission measurements:
- Core temperature 40.1°C (39–40.9): 3. Mean arterial pressure = (108 + 2 × 61)/3 ≈ 77 mm Hg (70–109): 0.
- Heart rate 136/min (110–139): 2. Respiratory rate 39/min (35–49): 3.
- FiO₂ is 0.73, so use the A–a gradient rather than PaO₂. Gradient 167 mm Hg (<200): 0. Arterial pH 7.32 (7.25–7.32): 2.
- Sodium 118 mmol/L (111–119): 3. Potassium 5.9 mmol/L (5.5–5.9): 1. Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL (0.6–1.4), without acute renal failure: 0.
- Hematocrit 43% (30–45.9): 0. WBC 24.2 × 10³/µL (15–39.9): 2. Neurologic points = 15 − GCS 12 = 3.
Acute physiology subtotal = 3 + 0 + 2 + 3 + 0 + 2 + 3 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 2 + 3 = 19. Age 19 (<45): 0. Immunosuppression after transplant with ongoing prednisone qualifies for 5 chronic health points on a nonoperative admission.
APACHE II = 19 + 0 + 5 = 24.
Final answer: 24
